query: The Prefect's Notebook {You have, it turns out, been walking on the lawn, which is for looking at. Bram Hollis has his notebook open and his pencil licked. "Rule nine," he says. "Demerit."|Bram again, and the notebook again, and the lawn again. "Rule nine," he says, with real joy.|Bram's pencil is already moving when you look up. He has a page with your name at the top now.} Argue the rule {You point out that rule nine was repealed in a year when the lawn caught fire. Bram checks. It was. He closes the notebook with great dignity.|You argue that you were looking at the lawn, very closely. Bram can't find the rule against that. He'll have one by Thursday.|You quote rule nine back at him, with the bit he left out. Bram goes pink and lets you off "this once, as a courtesy".} {Bram reads rule nine out loud to the whole courtyard, twice, and writes your name in capitals.|You argue; Bram quotes rule ten, which is about arguing. Two demerits.|Bram listens to your whole case, then writes it down as a separate offence.} Take the demerit and move on {You take it. Bram writes slowly, so everyone can see. "Next time," he says, and means it kindly, in his way.|Demerit. You walk off the lawn with your hands in your pockets. A first-year on a bench gives you a sympathetic look.|You take the demerit with a bow. Bram doesn't know what to do with a bow, and writes that down too.} Remind him he likes you {You say his name the way people say a friend's, with a little Glamour in it. Bram's pencil stops. He forgets, quite visibly, what he was writing.|A smile with a spell behind it. Bram closes the notebook, tells you to "watch the edges", and walks off frowning at himself.|Bram remembers liking you and not why. He lets you off, then follows you to the cloister to explain rule nine properly, which is its own punishment.}
